s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic skin eruption with atypical lymphocytic infiltrate
salient_findings: Multiple erythematous and violaceous plaques and nodules on the buttocks
Atypical lymphocytic infiltrate in the dermis with eosinophils and plasma cells
key_facts: Male patient in his 70s
Eruption duration of 5 years
Previous treatments with oral antibiotics, oral doxepin, and UV-B phototherapy failed
History of HSV-2 infection on the buttocks
Syphilis screen results were negative
Molecular analysis of the T-cell receptor gamma gene showed a weak clonal band
Repeat molecular studies showed no evidence of clonal rearrangement
Biopsy findings of dense infiltrate of atypical CD4+ small to medium-sized lymphocytes
Epidermotropism identified in second biopsy
Eosinophils and plasma cells present in the dermal infiltrate

s4.champion: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma

raw.champion: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma
raw.rationale: The presence of a dense infiltrate of atypical CD4+ small to medium-sized lymphocytes in the dermis, along with eosinophils and plasma cells, and the identification of epidermotropism in the second biopsy, are key features that support this diagnosis. The lack of evidence of clonal rearrangement in repeat molecular studies does not rule out this diagnosis, as it can sometimes be absent in this condition.

rejected.label: Mycosis fungoides
rejected.why: While mycosis fungoides is a type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, the absence of significant epidermotropism in the initial biopsy and the clinical presentation do not strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: This is a broad category that includes several types of lymphoma, but it is not specific enough to be the best diagnosis given the information provided.

rejected.label: Sézary syndrome
rejected.why: Sézary syndrome is a type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma that typically presents with widespread erythroderma, lymphadenopathy, and circulating malignant T-cells, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Primary cutaneous gamma-delta T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The biopsy findings of atypical CD4+ lymphocytes do not support a diagnosis of gamma-delta T-cell lymphoma, which typically involves gamma-delta T-cells.
